messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert P-32467 triggered for customer HarborView — VPC Private deployment (harborview-prod). symptom: sustained egress error spike to external analytics endpoint (10m avg error rate 26%). severity: SEV2. @dave please ack and triage.

dave (Oncall): acked. I'm on it. Paging netops and platform. @ben @carol — can you join? customer-ops is oncall for HarborView too.

ben (NetOps): On my way. Observing outbound HTTP 502/504s from tenant subnet 10.8.32.0/24 to analytics.hv-external.com (34.210.99.12). NLB in front of the egress NATs shows healthy, but target 34.210.99.12 failing healthchecks intermittently.

alice (SRE): Getting telemetry: per-tenant retries > 15% on dedicated pool dp-harborview, 95th latency +2000ms. KV-cache hit unchanged. Not a runtime CPU issue. Likely networking egress path.

carol (Platform): Stack: Private VPC -> Private NLB (egress) -> NAT GW in customer-managed subnet -> Internet. We run a per-tenant egress SG that only allows 443 outbound to customer-approved hosts. No recent SG changes in last 24h according to audit.

eve (Solutions): HarborView reports active user impact: EU customers seeing failures in data export. They say 20% of exports failing last 10m. They're trying fallback to batch but want live mitigation.

customer-ops: Confirmed. HarborView on support line, asking for ETA. They flagged compliance concern if we flip routing; want minimal config changes.

dave (Oncall): Triage plan: 1) Confirm NLB / NAT health 2) Check SG and route tables 3) If NAT saturation, fail traffic to alternate egress or enable temporary proxy 4) Notify customer and coordinate. Assigning tasks.

ben (NetOps): Running quick checks now.

ben (NetOps): `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:...hg-egress-tg` shows targets: 34.210.99.12 unhealthy (503), 35.196.77.44 healthy. Health reasons: HTTP_5XX_FROM_TARGET. But error rates not high for all targets.

ben (NetOps): NAT metrics: `CloudWatch: NAT-aggregated-ConnectionCount spike ~3x baseline, ConnectionTracked ~98%` — conntrack nearing table limit on nat-01 in us-east-1.

alice (SRE): conntrack saturation would produce intermittent failures. Do we have NAT autoscale? Private NAT is single AZ. If conntrack full we can circuit-break per-tenant egress to alternate pool.

carol (Platform): We have a standby egress pool (dp-standby) in another AZ with different NAT gw. Can we shift HarborView traffic there temporarily? That requires SG/route tweak in their VPC — risky but minimal downtime.

ben (NetOps): Quick mitigation: reduce conntrack by dropping long-lived idle connections. I can increase conntrack table size on nat-01 via SSM if allowed. Temporary change, low risk. Want approval.

dave (Oncall): Approve increase of conntrack limit as short-term. @carol prepare rollback plan and notify customer of potential 30s blip.

carol (Platform): Preparing runbook. Steps:

1) SSM run command to update /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max -> +50k on nat-01
2) Monitor conntrack_count and connection_errors
3) If still high, shift HarborView routing via route table update to dp-standby (will need to update route propagation and update NLB target group weights)
4) Rollback: revert nf_conntrack_max and route table.

ben (NetOps): Executing SSM now.

ben (NetOps): `aws ssm send-command --document-name "AWS-RunShellScript" --targets Key=instanceids,Values=i-0abcd1234 --parameters commands=['sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000']`

deploy-bot: SSM command c-7a3f executed on nat-01: status Success.

ben (NetOps): sysctl change applied. conntrack_max updated to 200k. Immediate drop in conntrack pressure observed.

alice (SRE): Metrics after change: conntrack_count fell from 98% to 45% over 90s. Retry rate for HarborView exports down from 26% -> 6% in last 3m. P95 latency back to +350ms. Good sign.

customer-ops: HarborView confirms partial recovery, exports improving. They still see sporadic failures — any plan for more durable fix?

carol (Platform): Medium-term: migrate HarborView to dp-standby (different AZ with dedicated NATs) and enable autoscale for NAT instances/gateways. Also propose adding per-tenant connection limits at our edge.

dave (Oncall): Agree. For now keep nf_conntrack_max increased for 2h, monitor. I'll page infra to schedule migration for a maintenance window.

alice (SRE): Running post-mit checks: NLB target health stable. DNS no changes. Security group rules untouched. No signs of security event.

ben (NetOps): Also identified one long-tail client that kept TCP connections OPEN for >20m causing conntrack churn. We asked HarborView to patch client timeout to 60s. They're on it.

eve (Solutions): Noting customer asks: 1) written RCA 2) options for hardening 3) temporary credit for impacted exports. I'll own comms.

customer-ops: HarborView rep appreciates quick action. Wants 2h status update then RCA next day.

dave (Oncall): Handoff to daytime oncall @alice for 2h observation window. I'll update incident P-32467 to status: mitigated -> monitoring.

alice (SRE): Taking over monitoring. Set alert to notify if error rate >10% for 5m. Adding runbook link to incident.

carol (Platform): I'll open a dedicated migration ticket: MIG-4521 to schedule dp-harborview -> dp-standby migration with expected ~5m cutover during maintenance. Also raising infra ticket to enable NAT autoscaling across private egress fleets.

ben (NetOps): Leaving a note: if conntrack re-saturates we will perform immediate route shift to dp-standby: Command sequence (for runbook):

```
# 1) register standby targets
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:...standby-tg --targets Id=ip,Port=443
# 2) adjust weights / deregister primary
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:... --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false
# 3) update route table to point to standby NAT
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-standby
```

dave (Oncall): Documenting timeline in P-32467. Current status: mitigated (conntrack increase) -> monitoring. Customer notified. Owners: carol (migration), ben (netops followup), alice (monitor).

customer-ops: HarborView support: "Thanks, exports recovering. We'll accept maintenance window. Please send RCA." :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P-32467 status changed to MONITORING by dave. Links: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/P-32467

alice (SRE): Leaving a final note before stepping off: keeping nf_conntrack_max elevated for 2h then reduce to baseline during low-traffic window. If we see >10% errors after reduction, escalate to route shift. I'll hand to daytime rotation.

dave (Oncall): Handed off. Closing coordination thread here. If anything spikes, ping #incidents and re-open P-32467.
